gsm.ctas

gsm.ctas runs the ctas clinical trial anomaly detection engine inside the gsm workflow framework, so that CTAS site scores appear alongside the usual KRIs in a standard gsm site report.

The two frameworks answer different questions. gsm KRIs count events against exposure – enrolment rate, AE rate, query age. CTAS instead compares the distribution of a site’s measurements against the rest of the study, and so detects patterns a rate-based metric cannot: values that are too consistent, too smooth over time, too rounded, or missing in a structured way. This package is the adapter that lets one report carry both.

Installation 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")

The gsm framework packages and ctas are declared in Remotes and will be pulled in automatically. They are Suggests, not Imports: the mapping and aggregation functions are usable on their own, and only the workflow layer needs the full framework.

Usage

gsm.ctas ships all four gsm workflow layers in inst/workflow/, so a full run is a sequence of RunWorkflows() calls over SDTM input:

library(gsm.ctas)

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(pharmaversesdtm::dm),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(pharmaversesdtm::vs),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(pharmaversesdtm::lb)
)

lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw,
  gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

lMapped <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lMappingWorkflows, lIngest)

lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores is then filtered by each metric workflow in 2_metrics, summarised into the gsm analysis contract, and rendered by the stock gsm.kri site report. The full path – including reporting and the rendered HTML – is in vignette("gsm-ctas").

How it fits together 

lRaw --Ingest--> lIngest --1_mappings--> lMapped --2_metrics--> lAnalysis
     --3_reporting--> Reporting_* --4_modules--> HTML report
Layer Contents
1_mappings DM, VS, LB, SITE, STUDY, plus CTAS_Input -> CTAS_SiteScores -> CTAS_Detail
2_metrics ctas0001-ctas0011, one per parameter family x CTAS feature
3_reporting Groups, Metrics, Results, Bounds
4_modules report_kri_site

The key structural point is that CTAS is an all-metrics-at-once engine. A single ctas::process_a_study() call scores every timeseries x feature x site, so it runs once, in 1_mappings/CTAS_SiteScores.yaml. Each metric workflow then merely filters that shared result down to one parameter family and one feature. Adding a metric is therefore a YAML change, not a code change.

Extending

Both common customisations are config-only and are documented in the vignette:

  • Thresholds are exposed the gsm-native way, through meta and ParseThreshold in each metric YAML.
  • New metrics are added by copying a metric YAML and changing the Feature, Domain and Transformation fields.

Related packages

Package Role
ctas The statistics engine
gsm.core Workflow execution
gsm.kri Report rendering
ctasapp Dashboard for drilling into a flagged site

The division of labour between the last two is deliberate: the gsm report detects signals, ctasapp investigates them. Combine_CTAS_Detail() and Write_CTAS_Detail() retain the timeseries-level detail that aggregation discards, for handoff to the dashboard.

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Please use the issue templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/.

Exported functions follow a stage-based naming scheme – Input_* (SDTM to CTAS input), Prepare_* (make values comparable), Analyze_* / Summarize_* / Flag_* (run CTAS and bridge into gsm), Combine_* and Write_* (assemble and export). Note that Transform_* is not used, as it carries a specific and different meaning within gsm itself.
